results.title: Implementation Science and Arts Outreach
results.content: In the following sections, we provide a detailed guide on using implementation science to improve arts outreach, addressing key dimensions of program design, community engagement, audience development, evaluation, policy impact, and organizational strategy. In many ways, arts outreach sits at the intersection of community education, public engagement, and cultural programming – areas where implementation science insights can be highly valuable. For instance, the RE-AIM framework (mentioned above) could be applied to an arts program: R (Reach) – who will we reach and how to maximize participation?; E (Effectiveness) – what outcomes do we expect (e.g., increased appreciation for art, improved wellbeing) and how to measure them?; A (Adoption) – what organizations or venues need to adopt this program (schools, community centers) and how to get their buy-in?; I (Implementation) – what training, materials, and supports are needed for fidelity?; M (Maintenance) – how will the program be sustained over time (funding, policy support, community ownership)?
